review_output: {"summary":"I reviewed the four core RichMenu modules against the supplied scope. Several things look correct: draft and account queries are scoped to the vendor, both claims use a compare-and-set on revision plus exact JSON, the created remote ID and the previous default are saved before the default switch, reconcile only marks synced when the default matches its own remote ID, and audits leave out links and credentials. I found four MAJOR problems and one MINOR: (1) a failure to save progress just before the default switch is recorded as set_default ambiguity, which locks the draft permanently even though no switch was ever sent; (2) reconcile also stays locked forever when a third-party menu is the default, even though that outcome is knowable; (3) a lease check after a confirmed switch saves a permanent 'conflict' even though the menu is live; (4) links supplied by the caller are saved without checking them against the strict envelope schema, which can make the draft permanently unreadable; and (MINOR) the caller is told 'conflict' after remote effects when sync loses ownership to reconcile. This covers the core half only. The persisted record also falsely claims a switch was attempted.","recommended_fix":"Keep the stage at a pre-switch value (for example check_current) until the set_default progress write has succeeded, then set stage='set_default' right before client.setDefault.
